title: Errors Store Document Schema
description: JSON Schema for the whole specs/errors.json document: an object holding an array of error records. Unlike specs/events.jsonl (strictly append-only), records here are mutated in place via fix_status transitions -- see context/formats/errors-format.md for the full prose contract, including the append/update CLI.

schema_version.description: Optional document-level schema version marker, reserved for future revisions. Not currently emitted by errors-append.sh.

errors.description: The list of error records. Empty array is valid -- this is the lazily-created / bootstrapped shape.

id.description: Unique error record ID. RECOMMENDED form: err_{timestamp_ms}_{random6} (mirroring events-schema.json's evt_ convention), always emitted by errors-append.sh. NOT enforced via pattern, so legacy err_001-style and err_{timestamp}-style ids from before this schema stay valid.

timestamp.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of when the error occurred.

type.description: Open, extensible string naming the specific kind of error. Not a closed enum -- new values may be added by future consumers. Common values documented in rules/error-handling.md: delegation_hang, timeout, validation_failed, status_sync_failure, file_not_found, parse_error, git_commit_failure, build_error, tool_unavailable, mcp_abort_error, delegation_interrupted, jq_parse_failure, plus source_store_defect (the subsumed source-store defect lane, added here as a documented type value rather than a new field).

severity.description: Closed 4-value severity taxonomy. critical = system unusable (stop, alert, require manual fix); high = feature broken (log, attempt recovery); medium = degraded function (log, continue with workaround); low = minor issue (log, ignore).

message.description: Short, human-readable one-line summary of what happened.

context.description: Union superset of every documented/observed context shape. NONE of the individual sub-fields are required -- no single writer populates them all.

session_id.description: The sess_{timestamp}_{random} value generated at command gate-in.

checkpoint.description: Lifecycle checkpoint name, e.g. GATE_IN, GATE_OUT, preflight, postflight.

agent.description: The subagent type/name involved, e.g. general-implementation-agent.

file.description: A relevant file path, e.g. the file being edited when the error occurred.

trajectory.description: Optional delegation-path context, present when the error is known to have occurred at a specific point in a multi-agent delegation chain.

delegation_path.description: Ordered list of delegation hops, e.g. ["orchestrator", "implement", "general-implementation-agent"].

failed_at_depth.description: 0-indexed depth into delegation_path where the failure occurred.

recovery.description: Optional recovery guidance attached at write time.

suggested_action.description: Human-readable suggested next step, e.g. "Run /implement 259 to resume from phase 2".

auto_recoverable.description: Whether the error is expected to resolve automatically on retry/resume.

fix_status.description: Closed 4-value lifecycle enum. unfixed -> in_progress -> fixed is the live transition path, driven by errors-append.sh's update subcommand. resolved is a DEPRECATED synonym for fixed, retained in this enum ONLY so already-written cross-repo data (observed live) stays schema-valid on read -- errors-append.sh never emits it, and its update subcommand REJECTS resolved as an input value with a message naming fixed as the replacement, so the deprecation cannot re-propagate into new writes.

fixed_date.description: Optional. Set by errors-append.sh update when fix_status transitions to fixed; defaults to the current time if not explicitly supplied.

fix_task.description: Optional. The bare (unpadded) task number whose implementation fixed this error, set by errors-append.sh update.

$comment: recurrence_count is intentionally NOT a persisted field. No writer has ever populated it, and /errors already computes recurrence at analysis time by grouping records on type -- see context/formats/errors-format.md's Reconciliation Decisions section for the full rationale. Keeping an unwritten field here would reintroduce the exact dead-field defect this schema exists to eliminate.
